proposals.title: Split tab-tracking write paths out of service_worker.js
proposals.body:
## Summary

`service_worker.js` is 1871 production lines against a 500-line budget, and its three longest functions (`groupTabs` 172, `recordInGroupTab` 130, `handleActiveTabsGroupChanges` 119) are over the 150-line entity budget. The url-* record write paths (`tabUpdates`, `urlUpdates`, `newUrl`, `recordAccess`) that the raw-URL-title fix had to touch live inside this file, which made each fix site slow to find and hard to test in isolation; the worker test harness has to strip imports and inject every helper by name.

## Key Decisions

- Move the url-* record tracking (`tabUpdates`, `urlUpdates`, `newUrl`, `recordAccess`, `getUrlKey`, `pruneVisits`) into `src/lib/worker/urlTracking.js` as pure-ish functions taking `getStorage` / `chrome.tabs.get` as parameters, like `src/lib/utils/urlRecordDisplay.js` already does for the display rules.
- Keep the chrome event listeners in `service_worker.js`; they become thin callers.
- Behaviour-preserving only: no logic changes in this plan.

## Implementation

1. Create `src/lib/worker/urlTracking.js` and move the functions listed above, injecting storage and tab access.
2. Update `service_worker.js` imports and the listener call sites (`onCreated`, `onUpdated`, `onActivated`).
3. Move the `describe('urlUpdates')`, `describe('newUrl')` and `describe('tabUpdates')` blocks from `service_worker.test.js` into `src/lib/worker/urlTracking.test.js`, calling the functions directly instead of through the `new Function` harness.
4. Remove the moved names from the harness parameter list in `service_worker.test.js`.

## Reproduction Test

Not a bug fix; the existing urlUpdates/newUrl tests (including `keeps a real title when the live tab reports its raw url`) must stay green after the move.
proposals.reason: service_worker.js is 1871 lines; the url-* record write paths this fix touched are spread across it.

proposals.title: Isolate component manifest missing in a fresh checkout breaks every component capture
proposals.body:
## What happened

In this checkout `.codeyam/generated/components.ts` (gitignored, read by the `codeyam:components` virtual module) did not exist. Every `/?isolate=<Name>` scenario rendered `No such component "<Name>" — register it with codeyam-editor editor isolate <Name>`. `register` for a new scenario with an interaction only reported `preview-interact: no element matched selector ".Url"` and `Candidate interactive labels: (none found on page)`, which pointed at the selector, not the missing manifest. `capture-state` was what finally showed the page text.

`codeyam-editor editor isolate --all` refused: `--all found no props modules under .codeyam/isolation-props (stack: chrome-extension-react) ... name the components instead`. I had to reconstruct the component list by hand from `.codeyam/harness/isolate.jsx` top-level keys; that missed 9 components (Favorites, Labels, LoadMeter, LoadMeterCaption, LoadPerTabNote, LoadProcesses, Search, Tabs, Triage). The following `recapture-stale` (281 scenarios, ~14 min) then recaptured 30 scenarios as the 'No such component' page, overwriting good committed screenshots, and only the distinct-capture collision check (111 colliding pairs) revealed it. A second targeted recapture fixed them.

## What would have helped

- `isolate --all` on query-param isolation stacks should rebuild the manifest from the component names scenarios actually reference (`isolate=<Name>` in `.codeyam/scenarios/*.json`), or from the harness's props map.
- The dev-server or capture pre-flight should detect a missing or incomplete manifest and regenerate it, since it is a derived, gitignored cache.
- A capture whose page is the harness's 'No such component' placeholder should fail that slug, not be saved as its screenshot.
- When an interaction finds no element and the page shows the placeholder, say so in the error instead of blaming the selector.
proposals.reason: A missing gitignored manifest made every component scenario render 'No such component', and a recapture then overwrote good screenshots with that error page.

proposals.title: Scenarios seeding absolute timestamps silently age out without a clock pin
proposals.body:
## What happened

`tabs-auto-closed-newest-first` and `tabs-auto-closed-newest-first-after-removal` seed `autoClosed` timestamps from 2026-10-02 and pin no `clock`. The app filters entries older than `MaxAutoClosedTime` against `Date.now()`, so by 2026-10-23 the Automatically Closed list rendered empty and the after-removal scenario's click target (`.Tabs-autoClosed .Url-removeBtn`) disappeared, failing its capture. `recapture-stale` listed them as `clock_drift_candidates` only after they had already been recaptured wrong, alongside 15 Favorites scenarios whose 'drift' was really the missing-manifest problem, so the signal was noisy. I pinned `"clock": {"now": "2026-10-02T01:00:00Z", "frozen": true}` on both by hand.

## What would have helped

- At `register` time, warn when a scenario's seeded data contains epoch-millisecond timestamps but no `clock` is pinned, and offer to pin `now` just after the newest seeded timestamp.
- An audit check for the same condition across existing scenarios, before they rot.
proposals.reason: Two Tabs auto-closed scenarios went empty three weeks after capture because nothing flagged their unpinned dates.

proposals.title: Fix undeclared tabId in associateProcess so per-tab process stats record
proposals.body:
## Summary

`associateProcess` in `service_worker.js` iterates with `for (tabId of tabIds)`, assigning to an undeclared `tabId`. The worker ships as an ES module (crxjs sets `"type": "module"`), which is strict mode, so this throws `ReferenceError: tabId is not defined` as soon as a process has a tab task. `processProcesses` then rejects before `update(updates)`, so neither per-tab process stats nor `processTotals` are persisted from the processes path. The test harness evaluates the worker in a sloppy-mode `new Function`, which hides the bug.

## Key Decisions

- Declare the loop variable: `for (const tabId of tabIds)`.
- Add a regression test that runs `associateProcess` under strict semantics, for example by adding `'use strict'` to the harness wrapper or by extracting `associateProcess` into `src/lib/worker/` like the url-tracking split, so the test sees what production sees.

## Implementation

1. Change the loop header in `associateProcess` in `service_worker.js`.
2. Make the `service_worker.test.js` harness strict, or move `associateProcess` and `updateTotals` into a worker module with injected `getTab` / `tabUpdates`, and test it there.
3. Confirm `associateProcess › fetches each task tab and merges its url updates` fails under strict mode before the fix and passes after.
proposals.reason: In the shipped module build this loop throws on every process sample, so per-tab CPU and memory stats are never saved.

proposals.title: Split tab-grouping paths out of service_worker.js
proposals.body:
## Summary

After the url-tracking split, `service_worker.js` is 1578 lines. The tab-grouping logic (`groupTabs`, `recordInGroupTab`, `handleActiveTabsGroupChanges`, `ejectAutoGroupedTab`, `dissolveDeletedLabelGroups`, `stampLabelMembership`, `urlKeyIsMember`, `mapColors`) is the largest remaining concern, and its tests still go through the `new Function` harness.

## Key Decisions

- Follow the `src/lib/worker/urlTracking.js` pattern: move the functions into `src/lib/worker/grouping.js`, pass chrome.tabs / tabGroups / storage and the worker Sets (`pendingUngroups`, `autoGroupedTabs`, `userDeletedLabels`) in as deps, and keep the listeners in the worker as thin callers.
- Behavior-preserving only.

## Implementation

1. Create `src/lib/worker/grouping.js` with the functions above and a deps object.
2. Build a `groupingDeps` object in `service_worker.js` and update the call sites.
3. Move the matching describe blocks from `service_worker.test.js` into `src/lib/worker/grouping.test.js`, and remove the moved names from the harness.
proposals.reason: service_worker.js is still 1578 lines against a 500-line budget; groupTabs, recordInGroupTab and handleActiveTabsGroupChanges are each over 100 lines.

proposals.title: reconcile-decide delete is silently not applied when the orphan shares its name with a live entry
proposals.body:
## What happened

I deleted the worker's duplicates of `siteKey`, `pruneVisits` and `isSearchEngineUrl`, whose glossary rows lived at `service_worker.js`. Rows with the same names exist at their canonical util files. `advance` reported 3 ambiguous orphans. `reconcile-decide --batch` with `"action":"delete"` reported `Recorded 3 decision(s)`, but the next `advance` re-raised the same 3 cases word for word, and `.pending-decisions.json` still held the deletes. I had to fall back to `glossary-remove <name> --file service_worker.js` for each one and delete the pending-decisions file by hand. `relocate-entities` then hit a related wall: it refused to move `getUrlKey` because a distinct same-named function exists in `urlDetails.js`, which also needed a manual remove-and-re-add with `collisionDisposition`.

## What would have helped

Decisions keyed by `(name, filePath)` instead of name alone, so a delete for the orphan at `service_worker.js` applies to that row. Or, failing that, a refusal at `reconcile-decide` time that says the name is ambiguous and prints the `glossary-remove --file` command, rather than recording a decision that can never apply.
proposals.reason: Recorded delete decisions for three same-named mirror entries, but the next advance re-raised the identical ambiguity.
